lead.headline: 40 big California water systems serving 4.2M people have no full sanitary inspection on EPA's file in 5 years
lead.number: 40 California systems, 4.22M people, mostly in LA, San Bernardino, Riverside and San Diego counties; 35 of the original 41 show no visit of any kind since mid-2021. Nationally 94 systems, 7.66M people, counted from each state's real data end.
lead.watch_out: All of this is absence in EPA's federal copy; New Jersey's gaps look like visits logged under another code, not missed surveys.

sources.page_context: completion rate in 2019. However, during 2020, the Covid19 shelter-in-place restrictions and social distancing requirements, contract tracer assignments, along with fire response and recovery efforts, have significantly reduced staffs’ ability to complete sanitary surveys. DDW’s state-wide average completion rate stands at 78% through the first three quarters of 2020 and is expected to drop for the first time 5 years. In response to COVID social changes, staff have been developing innovative measures to incorporate virtual water system inspections alongside the on-site sanitary surveys to attempt to complete as many as possible and fulfill our primary mission of monitoring water systems to protect public health.
